sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A BLOCK IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST IN THE LARGE-SCALE PATTERN ACROSS THE BRITISH COLUMBIA AND PACIFIC NORTHWEST COAST THROUGH THIS PERIOD. STRONGER WESTERLIES WILL REMAIN SPLIT AROUND THIS FEATURE ...BEFORE CONVERGING BETWEEN BROAD UPPER TROUGHING ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND EASTERN CANADIAN PROVINCES/NORTHERN TIER OF THE U.S. AND STRONG SUBTROPICAL RIDGING ACROSS THE MEXICAN PLATEAU INTO THE GULF OF MEXICO. ON THE NORTHERN PERIPHERY OF THIS RIDGE ...SEASONABLY WARM/MOIST AND POTENTIALLY UNSTABLE AIR WILL REMAIN WIDESPREAD FROM THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS THROUGH THE LOWER HALF OF THE MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO MUCH OF THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD. THIS INSTABILITY...COUPLED WITH FAVORABLE DEEP LAYER SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH A BROAD ZONE OF RELATIVELY STRONG WESTERLY MID- LEVEL FLOW...WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A CORRESPONDINGLY BROAD AREA WITH A RISK FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS TODAY. THIS WILL BE AIDED BY FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH A SERIES OF SHORT WAVE IMPULSES EMERGING FROM THE TROUGH IN THE SOUTHERN BRANCH OF THE SPLIT FLOW...ACROSS THE SOUTHWESTERN STATES.

sections.title: MID/LWR MS VALLEY INTO THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD
sections.text: MIXED LAYER CAPE OF 1500-3000 J/KG AND SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH 30-50 KT WESTERLY 500 MB FLOW WILL SUPPORT POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE STORMS OVER A FAIRLY BROAD AREA. HOWEVER...CONSIDERABLE UNCERTAINTY EXISTS CONCERNING THE DETAILS OF THE CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION...AND THE SEVERE THREAT IN POCKETS MAY BE CONSIDERABLY GREATER...OR SOMEWHAT LESS...THAN CURRENTLY INDICATED. FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH VORTICES EMBEDDED WITHIN A BROADER SCALE LOW AMPLITUDE SOUTHERN BRANCH TROUGH APPEAR LIKELY TO CONTRIBUTE TO CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ALONG AND SOUTH OF A STALLED FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS THE OHIO VALLEY INTO THE NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC COAST. AT THE SAME TIME...ANOTHER IMPULSE MIGRATING AROUND THE NORTHERN PERIPHERY OF THE SUBTROPICAL RIDGE SEEMS LIKELY TO CONTRIBUTE TO CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE NORTHERN GULF STATES. THIS COULD LEAVE A RELATIVE MINIMUM IN CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL ACROSS PARTS OF THE TENNESSEE VALLEY...AS ADDITIONAL STORMS FORM TO THE LEE OF THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS TODAY. REGARDLESS...SHEAR PROFILES WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR MID-LEVEL UPDRAFT ROTATION IN DISCRETE STORMS...WHILE ALSO CONTRIBUTING TO THE EVOLUTION OF GROWING STORM CLUSTERS THROUGHOUT THE AREA... WHICH WILL BE CAPABLE OF P

sections.title: SOUTHERN PLAINS INTO THE ARKLATEX
sections.text: STALLED FRONTAL ZONE ON THE NORTHERN PERIPHERY OF THE SUBTROPICAL RIDGE IS EXPECTED TO PROVIDE THE FOCUS FOR LATE AFTERNOON STORM DEVELOPMENT. STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT IN THE PRESENCE OF FAVORABLE SHEAR...BENEATH 30-50 KT WESTERLY 500 MB FLOW...ARE EXPECTED TO BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING VERY LARGE HAIL. ISOLATED TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE BEFORE A NOCTURNALLY STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL JET CONTRIBUTES TO STORM CONSOLIDATION AND UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A LARGE STORM CLUSTER NEAR THE RED RIVER INTO THE ARKLATEX THIS EVENING. THIS MAY BE ACCOMPANIED BY A FEW DOWNBURSTS AND A CONVECTIVELY GENERATED COLD POOL WITH STRONG WINDS ALONG ITS GUST FRONT BEFORE WEAKENING OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: FLORIDA
sections.text: MID-LEVEL CAPPING IS EXPECTED TO BE WEAK ENOUGH TO ALLOW FOR CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ALONG CONVERGING SEA BREEZES BY LATE AFTERNOON...IF NOT BEFORE. THIS MAY BE AIDED BY FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER IMPULSE TURNING SOUTH SOUTHWESTWARD AROUND THE EASTERN EDGE OF THE SUBTROPICAL RIDGE. WITH STRONG SURFACE HEATING INTO THE 90S EXPECTED ACROSS THE INTERIOR PENINSULA...THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES ARE EXPECTED TO BE FAVORABLE FOR LOCALIZED DOWNBURSTS AND CONVECTIVE GENERATED SURFACE COLD POOLS. AIDED BY 10-20 KT NORTHERLY MID-LEVEL WINDS...THERE APPEARS TO BE POTENTIAL FOR A GROWING CONVECTIVE CLUSTER AND CONSOLIDATING COLD POOLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING A SWATH OF DAMAGING WINDS ACROSS THE CENTRAL INTO SOUTHERN PENINSULA BY THIS EVENING.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: FAVORABLE DEEP LAYER SHEAR WITHIN A MOIST AND POTENTIALLY UNSTABLE UPSLOPE FLOW IS ONCE AGAIN EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE STORMS LATE THIS AFTERNOON...INCLUDING ISOLATED SUPERCELLS. MODELS SUGGEST THAT FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH A JET STREAK NOSING ACROSS THE CENTRAL ROCKIES WILL ENHANCE CONVECTION...AND COULD CONTRIBUTE TO THE EVOLUTION OF AN ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTER ACROSS EASTERN COLORADO AND WESTERN KANSAS BEFORE ACTIVITY WEAKENS LATE THIS EVENING. ..KERR/GRAMS.. 06/11/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: GENERALLY ZONAL FLOW REGIME WILL PERSIST TODAY ACROSS BULK OF THE CONUS BETWEEN LARGE-SCALE BROAD TROUGHING OVER CANADA AND AN EXPANSIVE SUB-TROPICAL RIDGE ACROSS MEXICO AND THE GULF AND ADJACENT GULF COAST STATES. THE BROAD BAND OF MODEST 30-40 KT MID-LEVEL FLOW BETWEEN THESE FEATURES STRETCHES FROM THE GREAT BASIN TO THE PLAINS AND OH VALLEY TO THE EAST/NORTHEAST. WITHIN THIS FLOW EXIST A PLETHORA OF WAVES/PERTURBATIONS ACROSS A VARIETY OF SCALES. AT THE SURFACE...A FRACTURED/SEGMENTED FRONTAL ZONE STRETCHES FROM HIGH PLAINS EAST OF THE ROCKIES SEWD AND THEN EWD ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS AND THEN ENEWD FROM THE OZARK PLATEAU TO THE OH VALLEY. SEVERAL FRONTAL WAVES...SOME CONVECTIVELY INDUCED/SUSTAINED... EXIST ALONG THIS BOUNDARY.

sections.title: MIDWEST/OH VALLEY/TN VALLEY TO CNTRL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: ONE OF THE MORE OBVIOUS LARGER-SCALE SHORT WAVE TROUGHS AND ITS ASSOCIATED SURFACE LOW EXIST ACROSS THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY THIS MORNING. A NUMBER OF MUCH SMALLER SCALE CONVECTIVELY GENERATED/ENHANCED VORTICES SURROUND THIS WAVE FROM MO TO OH/WV AND SOUTH TO TN. WHILE THERE IS CONSIDERABLE CLOUD COVER AND PRECIPITATION ASSOCIATED WITH THIS SYSTEM...THERE WILL NO DOUBT BE AREAS AND POCKETS OF GREATER DESTABILIZATION AS THE ENTIRE CIRCULATION DEVELOPS EWD ACROSS THE UPPER OH VALLEY/TN VALLEY AND CNTRL APPALACHIANS THROUGH THE DAY. LINES OF STORMS IN CYCLONIC ARCS SHOULD GRADUALLY INTENSIFY AS GREATER INSTABILITY IS REALIZED. ORGANIZING INFLUENCE WITH THE LOW AND FASTER FLOW WITHIN THE UPPER TROUGH SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO STORM PERSISTENCE WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL SPREADING FROM TN/KY EWD TO WV/PA THROUGH THE DAY AND INTO THIS EVENING.

sections.title: SRN PLAINS
sections.text: QUASI-STATIONARY OR SLOWER MOVING AREAS OF DIABATICALLY ENHANCED SURFACE LOW PRESSURE ARE FORECAST TO PERSIST ALONG FRONTAL ZONE/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY INTERSECTIONS FROM OK/TX ACROSS THE MS VALLEY AND INTO THE TN VALLEY. UNLIKE THE MIDWEST FRONTAL WAVE...THESE SURFACE LOWS WILL GENERALLY LACK LARGER SCALE UPPER-LEVEL SUPPORT WITH SHORT WAVE RIDGING SPREADING ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS TODAY. NEVERTHELESS...PERSISTENT LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND DESTABILIZATION NEAR THESE FEATURES...AND ALONG FRONTAL SEGMENTS...SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR SOME STORM DEVELOPMENT. MOST LIKELY SCENARIO IS THAT STORMS ACROSS TX WILL CONTINUE TO POSE SOME RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND HIGH WINDS GIVEN VERY MOIST AND INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS PRESENT ALONG THE FRONTAL SEGMENT SITUATED ACROSS NRN TX. THIS CONVECTION APPEARS TO BE BACKBUILDING THIS MORNING ON THE EDGE OF STRONG CAPPING FARTHER SOUTH. MODEST WLY FLOW AND MID LEVEL DRY LAYER MAY SUPPORT COLD POOL GENERATION AND EVENTUAL FORWARD PROPAGATION OF THIS ACTIVITY WITH WIND AND HAIL THREATS SPREADING EAST ACROSS PARTS OF AR/LA AND MS THROUGH LATER TODAY.

sections.title: CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: THE NEXT LARGER DISTURBANCE IN THE CONUS WAVE TRAIN WILL MOVE FROM THE WEST COAST TO THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST TODAY WHILE UNDERGOING GRADUALLY DEAMPLIFICATION. WEAK HEIGHT FALLS WITH THIS TROUGH WILL SPREAD ACROSS THE ROCKIES AND CONTRIBUTE TO ENHANCED LIFT ACROSS THE MOUNTAINS AND ALONG THE FRONT BACKED INTO THE HIGH PLAINS FROM WY/CO. STORM PERSISTENCE AND UPDRAFT STRENGTH ON AND EAST OF THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WILL AGAIN BE SUPPORTED BY MARGINALLY MOIST LOW LEVEL ELY/UPSLOPE FLOW AND STEEP LAPSE RATES ALOFT. INITIAL/DISCRETE UPDRAFTS WILL LIKELY TO ACQUIRE ROTATION GIVEN HELICITY-RICH ENVIRONMENT ENCOUNTERED NEAR AND EAST OF THE FRONTAL ZONE. ONE OR TWO ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS COULD BE SUSTAINED EWD ACROSS WRN SECTIONS OF NEB/KS GIVEN FAVORABLE FORCING FOR ASCENT AND POTENTIAL FOR AT LEAST WEAK LEE-CYCLONE DEVELOPMENT THROUGH TONIGHT. IN ADDITION TO SOME HAIL AND TORNADO POTENTIAL WITH THIS CONVECTION...A WIND DAMAGE THREAT COULD EVOLVE IF A SMALL MCS OR TWO CAN DEVELOPMENT AND PROPAGATE PREFERENTIALLY ESEWD ALONG INSTABILITY AXIS FROM ERN CO INTO ADJACENT KS/NEB. ..CARBIN.. 06/11/2009

sections.title: MIDDLE TN EWD TO THE SRN APPALACHIANS THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A WELL-DEFINED MCV IS MOVING EWD OVER MIDDLE TN AS OF LATE MORNING. THIS SYSTEM IS ACCOMPANIED BY A NARROW BELT OF 40-50 KT MID LEVEL FLOW...AND IS PRECEDED BY A MOIST AND MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. EXPECT THE CONVECTION WITH THE MCV TO PERSIST INTO THE AFTERNOON WHILE SPREADING EWD OVER ERN TN AND ADJACENT AREAS...WITH A CONTINUED THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL. ADDITIONALLY...THERE WILL BE THE POSSIBILITY OF ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADOES WHERE THE CONVECTIVE CLUSTER INTERSECTS AND MOVES EWD ALONG A RESIDUAL E-W OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS ERN TN...IN THE WAKE OF THE WEAKENING CLUSTER NOW APPROACHING THE BLUE RIDGE.

sections.title: S CENTRAL PA SWD INTO CENTRAL VA/NRN NC THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THE REMNANTS OF A WEAKENING OVERNIGHT MCS ARE CROSSING THE BLUE RIDGE AS OF 16Z...AND THIS SYSTEM WILL CONTINUE EWD ACROSS SRN PA/MD/CENTRAL VA/NRN NC THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON. MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE RATHER POOR OVER THE REGION /AOB 6 C/KM BASED ON 12Z SOUNDINGS/...BUT SOME SURFACE HEATING AND A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WITH DEW POINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S WILL RESULT IN SUFFICIENT DESTABILIZATION /MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J/KG FOR SEVERE STORMS...ESPECIALLY ACROSS VA AND NC. THE NWD EXTENT OF THE STRONGER DESTABILIZATION COULD BE LIMITED BY PERSISTENT CLOUDS FROM NRN VA INTO SRN PA. MEANWHILE...STRENGTHENING MID LEVEL FLOW ACCOMPANIES THE REMNANT CONVECTIVE SYSTEM MOVING OVER VA FROM THE W...AND IT APPEARS PROBABLE THAT NEW STORMS WILL FORM THIS AFTERNOON IN A N-S BAND ALONG THE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AS IT PROGRESSES EWD ACROSS THE PIEDMONT. DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT WITH BOWING SEGMENTS...THOUGH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: NW/N CENTRAL INTO E TX THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: ONGOING CONVECTION IN N/NE TX IS BEING MAINTAINED BY WAA ABOVE THE SHALLOW COLD POOL GENERATED BY OVERNIGHT AND EARLY MORNING STORMS. THE 12Z FWD SOUNDING SHOWED STRONG ELEVATED INSTABILITY /MUCAPE IN EXCESS OF 3000 J/KG/...WHILE OTHER SOUNDINGS TO THE S REVEALED A LITTLE STRONGER CAP. THERE IS SOME UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE SHORT-TERM EVOLUTION OF THE STORMS GIVEN AN EXPECTED WEAKENING OF THE SWLY LLJ THAT HAS BEEN FEEDING THIS CONVECTION. HOWEVER...DIURNAL WEAKENING OF THE CAP THROUGH DAYTIME HEATING AND NEW COLD POOL GENERATION COULD ALSO ALLOW STORMS TO ROOT CLOSER TO THE SURFACE AND BEGIN TO PROPAGATE SEWD AS AN MCS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. FARTHER W/NW...A SURFACE COLD FRONT IS SAGGING SWD ACROSS THE TX PANHANDLE INTO NW TX...WHERE THE BOUNDARY INTERSECTS THE WWD EXTENSION OF THE OUTFLOW FROM THE N TX STORMS. STRONG SURFACE HEATING AND A NARROW CORRIDOR OF UPPER 50S TO MID 60S BOUNDARY LAYER DEW POINTS COULD SUPPORT ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE FRONT FROM THE SE TX PANHANDLE ESEWD INTO NW TX. DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR AND INSTABILITY WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELLS...AND A TORNADO OR TWO COULD OCCUR WITH STORMS RIDING ESEWD ALON

sections.title: ERN CO/WRN KS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: MOIST POST-FRONTAL UPSLOPE WILL CONTINUE ACROSS CO TODAY AS LOW-LEVEL FLOW VEERS TO MORE ELY/SELY IN RESPONSE TO THE APPROACH OF A MID LEVEL TROUGH MOVING ENEWD FROM UT/AZ. LAPSE RATES ARE RELATIVELY POOR OVER THE HIGH PLAINS IN THE MOIST ENVIRONMENT...BUT DAYTIME HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEW POINTS IN THE LOW-MID 50S WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 500-1000 J/KG. THIS MODEST INSTABILITY...IN COMBINATION WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AOA 50 KT AND INCREASING LOW-LEVEL SHEAR LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF A FEW SUPERCELLS FORMING JUST E OF THE MOUNTAINS AND MOVING EWD ONTO THE PLAINS OF ERN CO. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MOST COMMON THREAT...THOUGH A COUPLE OF TORNADOES CAN ALSO BE EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING BEFORE CONVECTION BECOMES SLIGHTLY ELEVATED FARTHER E INTO WRN KS. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/11/2009

sections.title: LOWER AND MID OH VALLEY
sections.text: STORMS -- INCLUDING ISOLATED LOW-TOPPED SUPERCELLS -- HAVE EXPANDED IN COVERAGE ACROSS THE LOWER AND MID OH VALLEY REGION...ON SRN FRINGES OF A MID-LEVEL CIRCULATION NOW CENTERED OVER NRN INDIANA. WITH MIXED-LAYER CAPE NOW IN THE 1500 TO 2000 J/KG RANGE LIKELY TO LINGER INTO EARLY EVENING...STORMS SHOULD REMAIN STRONG/SEVERE FOR AT LEAST A FEW MORE HOURS BEFORE DIURNAL WEAKENING BEGINS. IN THE MEAN TIME...WITH LOCALLY-BACKED LOW-LEVEL FLOW -- PARTICULARLY ACROSS NRN KY/SRN INDIANA -- BENEATH MODERATE MID-LEVEL WLYS...SHEAR WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT ISOLATED SUPERCELLS...AND ASSOCIATED THREAT ISOLATED TORNADOES ALONG WITH GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL. ...MID MS/OH/TN VALLEYS EWD ACROSS THE APPALACHIANS TO THE ATLANTIC COAST STATES... SEVERAL BANDS OF CONVECTION ARE ONGOING ATTM FROM THE OH VALLEY/LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION SWD INTO THE SRN APPALACHIANS. WHILE STORMS CONTINUE DOWNSTREAM OF THE LOWER LAKES ACROSS NY...AND WITHIN AN ARCING BAND FROM NWRN PA INTO MD/VA/N CENTRAL NC...THE GREATER SEVERE POTENTIAL IS ONGOING WITHIN A SECOND ARC OF STORMS FROM ERN KY SWD ACROSS ERN TN/WRN NC AND INTO NRN GA/E CENTRAL AL. THIS CONVECTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH A COMPLEX MID-LEVEL SHORT-WAVE TROUGH NOW CRO

sections.title: TX/SRN OK
sections.text: STORMS ARE ONGOING ATTM ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHEAST TX SE OF THE METROPLEX...ALONG THE WRN/SWRN FRINGE OF AN EARLIER MCS. STORMS ARE ALSO INITIATING ATTM ACROSS NRN PORTIONS OF CENTRAL TX WHERE STRONG DESTABILIZATION CONTINUES...AND INCREASING CU IS INDICATED ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL TX NEAR AN ADVANCING DRYLINE...INTO THE S PLAINS NEAR THE DRYLINE/COLD FRONT INTERSECTION...AND THEN N INTO THE TX PANHANDLE NEAR AND TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE COLD FRONT. WITH A VERY UNSTABLE AIRMASS NOW IN PLACE...RESULTING FROM DAYTIME HEATING OF A MOIST /LOW TO MID 70S DEWPOINTS/ BOUNDARY LAYER BENEATH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP/ORGANIZE ACROSS THIS REGION. WITH LOW-LEVEL SLYS AHEAD OF THE DRYLINE ACROSS CENTRAL TX BENEATH 30 TO 40 KT MID-LEVEL WLYS...SHEAR IS SUFFICIENT TO ENHANCE CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION/SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT. WHILE INSTABILITY IS WEAKER NEAR/N OF THE FRONT ACROSS PARTS OF THE TX S PLAINS AND INTO THE PANHANDLE...STRONGER SHEAR -- AIDED BY BACKED LOW-LEVEL FLOW -- SUGGESTS AT LEAST A LIMITED SEVERE THREAT ACROSS PARTS OF THIS REGION. ALONG WITH THE THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED TORNADOES ACROSS CENTRAL TX...STORMS SHOULD ORGANIZE INTO ONE OR

sections.title: ERN CO/SERN WY/WRN KS/PARTS OF SWRN NEB
sections.text: STORMS ARE ONGOING ACROSS THE CENTRAL ROCKIES...AND HAVE BEGUN DEVELOPING ACROSS THE CO FRONT RANGE AND INTO SERN WY WHERE MODEST DESTABILIZATION /MIXED-LAYER CAPE AOB 750 J/KG/ AND WEAK UPSLOPE FLOW ARE INDICATED. STORMS SHOULD CONTINUE TO DEVELOP THROUGH THE AFTERNOON WITHIN MODESTLY-MOIST/DESTABILIZING AIRMASS...AND WITH AMPLE MID-LEVEL WLYS ATOP BACKED LOW-LEVEL FLOW...ORGANIZED/SUPERCELL STORMS ARE ANTICIPATED. ALONG WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR HAIL AND/OR LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS...ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH STRONGER CELLS THROUGH MID-EVENING. WITH TIME...MODELS SUGGEST THAT AN INCREASING SELY LOW-LEVEL JET WILL ALLOW STORMS MOVING OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN TO ORGANIZE INTO ONE OR TWO CLUSTERS...AND PROPAGATE SEWD ACROSS WRN KS -- AND POSSIBLY SWRN NEB...AND EVENTUALLY SPREAD INTO S CENTRAL KS AND ADJACENT NRN OK LATE. WHILE THE AIRMASS ACROSS THIS REGION WILL STABILIZE WITH TIME...A LOW-PROBABILITY SEVERE THREAT COULD LINGER WITH THIS CONVECTION THROUGH THE END OF THE PERIOD. ..GOSS.. 06/11/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1139 AM CDT THU JUN 11 2009/
